title: Anguilla vs Antigua: Which Should You Visit?
verdict: If you're chasing unparalleled tranquility, pristine beaches, and a 'quiet luxury' vibe, Anguilla is your pick, budget for $600-$1200+ per day. faq.question: Which island is better for a honeymoon?
faq.answer: Anguilla generally edges out Antigua for honeymoons due to its focus on luxury, seclusion, and intimate dining experiences. Its quiet, romantic atmosphere and exceptionally beautiful beaches are perfect for couples seeking an exclusive, peaceful escape. Antigua is also great, especially if you want more activities or a lively resort experience, but Anguilla specializes in 'romance and relaxation'.

faq.question: Which is better for families with kids?
faq.answer: Antigua is often a better choice for families. Its wider range of activities like ziplining, Stingray City, and more varied beach options cater well to different age groups. Accommodation options are also more diverse, including many family-friendly all-inclusive resorts. Anguilla is beautiful for families who prioritize quiet beach time, but offers fewer dedicated 'kid-friendly' attractions.

faq.question: Can I visit both Anguilla and Antigua in one trip?
faq.answer: Yes, absolutely! If you have 10-14 days, it's a fantastic combo. Fly into Antigua (ANU) for 5-7 days of exploring, then take a short regional flight (e.g., LIAT or private charter) to Anguilla (AXA) for another 5-7 days of pure relaxation. It provides a wonderful contrast of activity and tranquility.

faq.question: What's the best time of year to visit either island?
faq.answer: The peak season for both islands is typically from December to May, offering dry, sunny weather and comfortable temperatures (mid-70s to mid-80s Fahrenheit). This is also when prices are highest. The hurricane season runs from June to November, with September and October being the riskiest. Shoulder seasons (late May/early June and November) can offer good weather and lower prices.

faq.question: Which island has better snorkeling/diving?
faq.answer: Both islands offer decent snorkeling and diving, but Anguilla generally has a slight edge for clearer waters and healthier reefs, particularly around its offshore cays like Prickly Pear and Dog Island. Antigua has good spots too, especially around Cades Reef and the Pillars of Hercules, but Anguilla's pristine environment often results in better visibility and marine life encounters.

faq.question: Are there direct flights from the US/UK to both?
faq.answer: Antigua (ANU) offers numerous direct flights from major hubs in the US (JFK, MIA, ATL) and the UK (LHR, LGW). Anguilla (AXA) typically requires a connection, most commonly via St. Maarten (SXM) followed by a ferry, or via San Juan (SJU) with a regional flight. Direct access is much easier for Antigua.

faq.question: Which island has better shopping?
faq.answer: Antigua offers more diverse shopping opportunities, particularly in St. John's, where you'll find duty-free shops, local craft markets, and boutiques. English Harbour also has some nice shops catering to the yachting crowd. Anguilla's shopping scene is much more limited, focusing primarily on resort boutiques and a few local art galleries, reflecting its quiet, understated luxury.

faq.question: What's the primary language spoken on each island?
faq.answer: English is the official language spoken on both Anguilla and Antigua. While local dialects and accents may vary, English-speaking travelers will have no communication barriers on either island. The friendliness of the locals on both islands makes interactions easy and enjoyable.
